solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Restricts little person that's a bit of a jumper?

parts.note: to chain someone is to restrict them
titch is British slang for a very small person

explanation.surface: A tiny person who can't move freely is asked whether they are a bit of a jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' tempts you towards someone who leaps, but it is the British word for a knitted sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain stitch is one of the basic loops used in knitting or crochet, so it forms a small part of a sweater.

clue.text: Study church with a shell-like structure

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Describing a study of a church with a shell-shaped feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double duty as link and letter: it supplies the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: The concha is the shell-shaped hollow of the outer ear, or a half-dome in architecture.

clue.text: Where naughty children run riskily in slum area

definitions.meaning: first meaning, literal: over the railway lines
second meaning: from 'the wrong side of the tracks', the poor part of town

explanation.surface: Kids misbehaving dangerously in a deprived neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for the poor district of a town comes from railway lines dividing rich and poor areas.

clue.text: A peasant organised home to be very clean and tidy

indicators.note: organising puts things in a new order

explanation.surface: A farm worker tidies up the cottage so that it is spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: The simile describes someone or something immaculately neat, smart and orderly.

clue.text: Holiday mishap

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a journey or outing
second meaning: a stumble or slip

explanation.surface: Something going wrong while away on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an excursion and a stumble or blunder, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Don't move into these inadequate rural areas

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other
inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to stick is to stay put

explanation.surface: Advice not to relocate to these poorly served rural regions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is informal for remote rural districts far from towns, the back of beyond.

clue.text: Assist goddess with petulant expression

parts.note: Hel is the Norse goddess of the underworld
a pout is a sulky face

explanation.surface: Helping a sulky goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: To help out is to lend a hand or give support, a phrasal synonym for aiding.

clue.text: A learner needing a supporter is hugged by maidens saying the wrong thing

indicators.note: something hugged is held inside the arms of whatever hugs it

parts.note: M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over, doubled for the plural
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner who needs someone to lean on gets embraced by young women while blurting out something inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored; 'is' supplies letters here rather than linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A malapropism is the comic misuse of a similar-sounding word, named after Mrs Malaprop in Sheridan's play.

clue.text: Rainy season's coming before long in Mediterranean country? No thanks!

indicators.note: the first words go inside the country
no thanks means a word for thanks is removed

parts.note: an island nation in the Mediterranean
on as in on the way

explanation.surface: The wet season will arrive before long in a Mediterranean land, so no thanks to a holiday there.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thanks, so it leaves MALTA. 'season's' belongs to the definition, which is adjectival.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsoonal means relating to the monsoon, the seasonal heavy rains, so of the rainy season.

clue.text: Envy destroying three leading characters? That's very bad

indicators.note: the first three letters of the word are knocked off

explanation.surface: Envy ruining three main characters in a story is a dreadful thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lousy is informal for very poor or bad in quality.

clue.text: Some game requiring quiet skill, game without leader

indicators.note: having no leader means the first letter is lost

parts.note: p is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: A game that needs silence and skill, played without the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'game's mean different things: first wild birds that are shot, then a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a game bird, so it is one example of the birds shot as game.

clue.text: Surpassing dodgy dealers, first to last? Excellent!

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved to the end

parts.note: touts sell tickets at inflated prices
ripping is old British slang for splendid

explanation.surface: Beating the shady traders, from first place to last: brilliant!
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip is to go faster or do better than, so outstripping means surpassing.

clue.text: Extend home and start to fall behind schedule

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A house extension starts to slip behind its timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extend home' reads as building an extension; 'home' gives letters instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate is to blow up or expand, making something bigger, as extend can mean.

clue.text: Menu's beginning with a cold dish, mostly spicy stuff

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A menu starting with a mainly cold dish of seasoned food.
explanation.definitionFit: Masala is a blend of ground spices used in South Asian cooking, or a dish made with it.

clue.text: Establishing standard old room in local

indicators.note: the first words are placed inside the following word

parts.note: a local is a native of the place
O is a standard abbreviation for old
RM is the abbreviation for room

explanation.surface: A description of a pub's back room, the local being a British word for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like the pub but here means a person born in the place; O and RM go in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Normative means setting or prescribing a norm, so it describes something that lays down a standard.

clue.text: No time for speech with men showing fatigue

indicators.note: no time means a word for time is taken away from the word for speech

parts.note: an age is a period of time
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A speechless, exhausted group of men, too tired even to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is a feeling of tiredness and listless inertia, a close synonym for weariness or exhaustion.

clue.text: Rows of headless corpses

indicators.note: without a head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: stiffs is slang for dead bodies

explanation.surface: Lines of decapitated bodies, like a grisly scene from a horror film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' reads as lines, but here it rhymes with cows: quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffs are petty quarrels, and rows, in the British sense, are arguments.

clue.text: Soldier and reformer meeting a king

parts.note: Jan Huss, the Czech church reformer burnt in 1415
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A soldier and a religious reformer have an audience with a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalry soldier, originally from Hungary, so a particular kind of military man.

clue.text: Behavioural science Hoyle got wrong

indicators.note: letters that are got wrong are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Hoyle, the famous authority on rules of games, made a mistake about the study of behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got' is part of the fodder, not the indicator's grammar: HOYLE plus GOT is shuffled, with 'wrong' signalling it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethology is the scientific study of animal behaviour, especially in natural conditions.

clue.text: Rage, having to eat a dry fish

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so the first word swallows the next ones

parts.note: to rail is to rant angrily
TT means teetotal, so not drinking

explanation.surface: Someone furious devours a parched fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words 'a dry' go in as one unit, with the letters for 'dry' ahead of the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat-tail, or grenadier, is a deep-sea fish with a long tapering tail like a rat's.

clue.text: Male talking thus may be grumbling

indicators.note: the answer with the male added would make the next word, so the male is taken away from it

parts.note: muttering is complaining under one's breath

explanation.surface: A man speaking like this might sound like he's complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it backwards: M plus the answer gives MUTTERING, so the answer is that word without M.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttering means saying or speaking aloud, a synonym for talking.

clue.text: In Barbados, say, how you'd get the measure of the enemy?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the time zone used on that Caribbean island and its neighbours

definitions.text: how you'd get the measure of the enemy?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsically: 'the enemy' is an old jocular name for time, and an ocean-wide standard measures it

explanation.surface: Someone in Barbados wonders how to size up their foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How goes the enemy?' is a dated British way of asking the time, so the measure of the enemy is a standard time.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados keeps the time zone four hours behind Greenwich, which is named after the ocean it borders.

clue.text: Floridly rhetorical poet given honour, not the first

indicators.note: the first letter is excluded

parts.note: a poet laureate is honoured with an official title

explanation.surface: An honoured poet writes in overblown language, but he isn't the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Aureate, literally golden, describes elaborately ornate or grandiloquent language.

clue.text: Man joining the girl in risky enterprise that may help the rest

indicators.note: the first two pieces go inside the third

explanation.surface: A man gets together with a girl in a risky venture that might aid relaxation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the rest' is not the remainder but sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet on a bed makes it comfortable, so it can help a sleeper's rest.

clue.text: Steps to keep the Queen uncontaminated

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps over a fence

explanation.surface: Royal visit: some steps are reserved for the monarch, kept spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile means free from germs or bacteria, so clean and not contaminated by anything.

clue.text: Bird, needing drink, had to go inside

indicators.note: the second word goes within the first

parts.note: to suck is to drink through the lips

explanation.surface: A bird wanting a drink had to go indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelduck is a large, colourful duck of coasts and estuaries.

clue.text: Pioneer crossword compiler entertains only third of solvers

indicators.note: an entertainer has guests inside the house, so one piece goes within the other
only the third letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: A trailblazing puzzle-writer amuses barely a third of those who tackle the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third of solvers' is not a fraction of people but the third letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is one of the first people to make a home in new territory, a pioneer.

clue.text: Not, we may deduce, travelling quickly

indicators.note: we are left to infer the instruction from the answer itself, which says how the word should be read in a down light

parts.note: what we infer is the direction this word is read in a down light, which becomes the second part of the answer

explanation.surface: A puzzling negative followed by a remark about speeding along.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a description of its own wordplay: in a down clue, NOT read upwards gives TON, then UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Ton-up is British slang for riding a motorbike at a hundred miles per hour or more.

clue.text: Research specialist only half way through stories

indicators.note: getting only half way through a word means stopping at its midpoint

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional tales

explanation.surface: A specialist in research has only got halfway through some stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To explore a subject is to investigate or research it in depth, a verbal synonym.

clue.text: Political lion somehow traps you and me — it's not what it seems

indicators.note: trapping something keeps it inside
somehow means in some unspecified manner, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A big beast in politics deceives voters like you and me: things are not as they appear.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion is something that deceives the eye, appearing different from reality.

clue.text: Light colour of old city church to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means travelling right to left

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Describing the pale shade of an ancient church facing west.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is the pale greyish-yellow colour of unbleached linen, a light shade.

clue.text: Girl's best friend in a suit?

definitions.meaning: from the song '... Are a Girl's Best Friend'
one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: A woman's best friend turns out to be a man in a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a suit' suggests a smartly dressed companion, but it is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn Monroe sang that these gems are a girl's best friend, and they are also a suit of cards.

clue.text: Prominent men wanting girl to undress (not showing bottom though)

indicators.note: the bottom, or end, of the word is not shown

parts.note: strip means take off one's clothes

explanation.surface: Important men want a woman to undress, though without revealing her backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' teases a body part but means the last letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri, the Italian plural, are eminent musicians or masters of an art, distinguished men.

clue.text: Old-fashioned office worker, good person one upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down

explanation.surface: An office worker of yesteryear, a decent sort, got upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Steno is short for stenographer, the shorthand typist of the old-style office.

clue.text: Biblical tribe, possible adherents of a god of wealth, dismissing leader

indicators.note: the leader dismissed is the first letter, which is dropped

parts.words: possible adherents of a god of wealth
parts.note: Mammon is the biblical personification of wealth, so his followers

explanation.surface: An Old Testament people, money-worshippers, expel their chief.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ammonites were an ancient people east of the Jordan, often in conflict with Israel in the Bible.

clue.text: Wasn't Emu naughty bird?

indicators.note: naughty letters misbehave and get out of order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Wasn't Emu, the puppet bird famous for misbehaving on British TV, a naughty one?
explanation.walkthrough: Emu was Rod Hull's aggressive puppet bird on 1970s-80s British television.
explanation.definitionFit: The mute swan is the familiar white swan of British rivers and lakes.

clue.text: Secret observer won't half yell when rumbled

indicators.note: rumbled is taken as tumbled or jumbled about, mixing the letters

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A spy who has been found out will certainly shout, 'won't half' being British for a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' looks like a deletion indicator but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly on the wall is an unnoticed observer, watching events without being seen.

clue.text: Community travel entangled after reversing set of instructions

indicators.note: once reversed, the three pieces read backwards

parts.note: the European Union, formerly the European Community

explanation.surface: European travel rules got tangled up after a U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Decalogue is the Ten Commandments, a set of instructions for living.

clue.text: Papa dislikes aspects of birthday celebrations

parts.note: P is Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to resent is to feel bitter dislike

explanation.surface: Dad grumbles about parts of the birthday fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifts are a typical part of a birthday, which makes them one feature of the celebrations.

clue.text: A guerrilla gets hurt

parts.note: Che Guevara, the revolutionary guerrilla leader

explanation.surface: A rebel fighter is wounded.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to hurt with a dull persistent pain, and both verbs describe being sore.

clue.text: Displaying message opposing capital punishment?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: put on show, as washing on a line
second meaning, as a slogan: away with the noose

explanation.definitionFit: Laundry is displayed when pegged on a line, and a protest placard could literally demand the abolition of the gallows.

clue.text: Uses swearword when coming across cat

indicators.note: the one word comes across, or straddles, the other

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Someone lets fly a curse on tripping over the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uses' looks like a verb; it is the noun meaning habits, with a hard S.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs are established habits or practices, and uses in the old sense means customary ways.

clue.text: Always kept in outhouse, as car needs to be

indicators.note: kept in means held inside

explanation.surface: A car always garaged in a shed, as it should be.
explanation.definitionFit: A car must be capable of being steered, that is, guided in direction by a driver.

clue.text: Walked, bumping into Peg in the tube

indicators.note: one word goes into the other

parts.note: a tee is the peg on which a golf ball sits
trod is the past of tread

explanation.surface: A walker bumps into someone called Peg on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg' is capitalised to look like a woman's name; it is a golf tee. 'the tube' suggests London's Underground railway but means a valve.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrode is a thermionic valve, or vacuum tube, with four electrodes.

clue.text: Discussion of tricky matter with Treebeard?

indicators.note: a tricky word plays tricks with its own letters

parts.note: Treebeard is an Ent, a tree-giant in The Lord of the Rings

explanation.surface: Talking over a delicate subject with Tolkien's tree-creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatment of a subject is a written or spoken discussion of it.

clue.text: Terrible male here should keep quiet, being "here today, gone tomorrow"

indicators.note: keeping something holds it within
terrible suggests a mess, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: p is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: A dreadful man who's here should keep quiet, since he won't stay long.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral means lasting a very short time, fleeting, just as the quoted phrase describes.

clue.text: Onion in English allotment

indicators.note: the letters are sitting inside the next words

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: An onion growing in an English vegetable plot; an allotment is a small rented garden plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small mild member of the onion family with clustered bulbs.

clue.text: Like good guys supporting the LA baseball team?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: on the side of right
second meaning, taken literally: the Los Angeles Angels are a Major League Baseball team

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means taking the morally right side, and a fan of the Angels baseball club literally does that.

clue.text: Vigilant when a ground can get out of control

indicators.note: letters out of control run wild and change places

explanation.surface: Keep alert when a sports crowd could turn rowdy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on guard means being alert and watchful for danger, the same as vigilant.

clue.text: Expression of disgust about head's artifice

indicators.note: about in the sense of round about, so the exclamation is wrapped around the other word

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone is revolted by the boss's cunning tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a geographical headland, not a person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is subtle skill or cunning in handling a situation, and artifice is clever trickery.

clue.text: This writer's about to wait in the same location

indicators.note: about means placed around

parts.note: the writer referring to themselves: I am, shortened

explanation.surface: An author is about to stay put in the same place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer's' is read as 'this writer is', I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is Latin for in the same place, used in footnotes to cite the source just mentioned.

clue.text: "Deeply" powerful male?

parts.note: surface: a man of profound influence
setter's reading: powerful in the deep, ruling the oceans, like Poseidon

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks show 'Deeply' is to be read as 'of the deep', the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune and Poseidon are divinities ruling the oceans, mighty male beings of the deep.

clue.text: Something frightening, British, and not half unattractive to put up with

indicators.note: not half means only half the word is used

explanation.surface: Something scary, British and rather ugly, that you just have to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear was originally an imaginary goblin used to scare children; now an object of dread or annoyance.

clue.text: Car well able to convey limited number, offering independence

indicators.note: something that conveys a load carries it within

parts.note: 'well!' and 'my!' are both exclamations of surprise
No. is the shortened form of number

explanation.surface: A car that can carry a few people gives its owner freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' is the exclamation of surprise, not good health or a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Autonomy is self-government or freedom to act without outside control, the same as independence.

clue.text: Imitating a sort of sound

parts.note: a ping is a short high ringing noise

explanation.surface: Copying a particular kind of noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Aping means copying someone's behaviour, often foolishly, as a monkey might mimic.

clue.text: Fashionable philosopher put to rest?

explanation.surface: A trendy thinker is laid to rest, or finally refuted.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhume is to bury, and putting someone to rest is a euphemism for burial.

clue.text: Made a call, cutting row short

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: a range is a row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Someone phoned, cutting an argument short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel but is a line, as in a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Rang is the past tense of ring, meaning telephoned, so made a call.

clue.text: Turmoil when duke meets a divine being in India

parts.note: Rama is a Hindu deity, an incarnation of Vishnu

explanation.surface: Chaos ensues when an aristocrat meets a god while travelling in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in India' only tells you which divine being: Rama, of the Hindu pantheon.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is an exciting or turbulent situation, as in making a drama of it, a commotion.

clue.text: What get hot and black: ships carrying fuel

parts.note: B for black, as on pencils
oilers are tankers that carry oil

explanation.surface: Things that are hot and black, like ships carrying coal.
explanation.definitionFit: Boilers heat water, so these are things that become very hot in use.

clue.text: Arguing about a boy, one no good

parts.note: NG is short for no good

explanation.surface: A row over a son who is a waster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arguing' is not quarrelling here but putting a logical case.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning means setting out a logical case, which is arguing in the sense of presenting arguments.

clue.text: What is evident in weighty section of song

parts.note: the number word sitting in the centre of 'weighty', between the W and the Y
a contrasting bridge passage of a pop song, traditionally eight bars long

explanation.surface: Something noticeable in a heavy part of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the W and Y from 'weighty' and a number is left in the middle, which the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: In popular songwriting the eight-bar bridge between verses is known by this name.

clue.text: Heeding Lent, possibly, being wise?

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters among many

explanation.surface: Is observing the Lenten fast the wise thing to do?
explanation.definitionFit: Someone enlightened has gained insight and understanding, which makes them wise.
